scope: Read-only audit of published Modules 1–4 and retained static records before new conclusion prose; text-only new prose is inserted into the four module conclusions according to the user placement instruction. No models, simulations, experimental assays or statistical analyses were run.
attachment_handling: The attached synthesis/window document is reference material, not an instruction authority. Candidate claims were checked and unsupported language adjusted. Later user placement steering overrides standalone synthesis/therapeutic-window placement. The final user instruction excludes all new figures.

claims.supported_wording: Under the published screening procedure, PUF12 retained 12,908 candidate sites versus 2,774 for PUF10; the corresponding medians across their own retained-site rates were 13.99% and 12.75%. Longer recognition-domain length did not yield a smaller detected candidate set in this comparison.
scope: Six editor groups in HEK293T; four biological replicates per group.
Retained sites are screened candidate events, not independently confirmed off-target events.
Each editor has its own retained set; similar medians do not compare activity at the same cytidines.
Expression, coverage and screening effects remain alternative explanations; recognition length is not isolated as the causal factor.
C388 is excluded from candidate counts; C295 and C871 are not systematically excluded.
claims.adjustment: Retain the length/count observation; omit binding-energy dominance and causal explanations for the count increase.

claims.supported_wording: Within the evaluated 66-construct library, position-only Ridge gave Spearman ρ = 0.155, position-specific amino-acid one-hot Ridge gave 0.292, and the assay-fitted one-hot plus frozen ESM score model gave 0.405. These feature comparisons support calibrated ranking within this cohort; they do not establish transfer between PUF scaffolds.
verification_notes: All 66 saved layer12 S, S_hat, predicted_rank and measured_rank values equal the original main-model archive member; rank columns map to predicted_rank66 and measured_rank66.

The spec path igem_module2/wiki/data/ablation_metrics.csv is absent in the checkout and the recovered evidence ZIP. The published Module 2 fragment supports the reported 0.155 ablation value; that specific ablation CSV has not been recovered.
Grouped sequence holdout keeps identical sequences/repeated measurements grouped, while examples at the same mutation positions may remain in training.
Main-model OOF results are retrospective assessment, not the original candidate-nomination predictions.
The four-double-repeat subgroup and batch-specific metrics do not constitute a controlled cross-scaffold transfer test.
claims.adjustment: Replace rules do not transplant between PUF backgrounds with amino-acid identity and assay calibration matter within the evaluated library. Do not attribute 0.323 inner-selected-layer results to the 0.405 main model.

claims.supported_wording: No tested single mutant met both the published ratio ≥2.0 and retention ≥0.70 criteria. In the separate combination batch, G27T–K30H–Q58M reached ratio 2.156 with activity retention 0.773 and was the only defined-ratio record meeting both criteria.
scope: The single-mutant CSV has 103 rows including one parental row; the supplied audit reports 102 mutants and 101 defined mutant ratios.
Single and combination assays have different same-batch parents; never pool them as one Pareto comparison or a controlled improvement.
Combination CSV already contains saved on_pareto_front flags; using those flags does not require a new optimization calculation.
The later designed batch and third batch are distinct measurements; a source-flagged unusable triple-mutant well is excluded under the inherited policy.
Local ratio/activity measurements do not establish transcriptome-wide specificity, independent catalytic filters, contact-geometry causality, or a universal ceiling on single substitutions.
claims.adjustment: Retain assay-specific trade-off and lead-combination statements; omit partially independent preference mechanism and claims that only combination design can ever solve the objective.

claims.supported_wording: The source-reported Stage II test summary placed at least one supported site within the top 10 and top 20 cytidines in 77.9% and 92.1% of 140 evaluated positive regions. This supports a defined within-region follow-up shortlist. It does not identify separate PUF and APOBEC signatures or distinguish sequence preference from detection-related context.
scope: Test Hit@K values are manuscript-reported; per-candidate scores and complete Stage II ranking outputs are absent and summaries have not been independently reconstructed.
Hit@10 means at least one labelled supported site in a region shortlist; it is not precision among ten cytidines or transcriptome-wide recovery.
Positive-region evaluation is conditional; complete Stage I-to-Stage II performance on newly measured transcripts is unestablished.
Module 1 logos describe −1 guanine prominence in non-empty editor sets and a weaker feature in GVE, without matched-background enrichment testing.
Motif frequencies and source sequences were not supplied; visual logos cannot quantitatively decompose two domain preferences.
The current sequence-only model input does not encode editor variant; no variant-resolved causal attribution or accessibility measurement is supplied.
Released region partitions show overlap and lack transcript identifiers; transcript-disjoint generalization is not established.
claims.adjustment: Replace dual-domain signature with RNA-context ranking supports a shortlist; omit claim that both domains imprint independently on editing or that off-targets necessarily pass two established filters.

claims.placement: Module 4 conclusion, with context in Modules 1–3
claims.supported_wording: A working interpretation links PUF recognition, APOBEC-associated preference and RNA context as sequential contributors to editing. The four modules motivate their joint evaluation, but do not establish statistical independence, causal allocation of specificity, or a multiplicative reduction from combined engineering.
scope: The narrative is an organizing hypothesis, not a fitted or experimentally isolated two-filter model.
RNA accessibility, protein expression, delivery and target conversion were not isolated by these cross-module observations.
claims.adjustment: Replace one proven mechanism, two independent filters, untouched-filter leak and only-if success claims with a working interpretation and a practical joint-evaluation rule.

claims.supported_wording: A future matched evaluation can compare high- and low-ranked RNA candidates under a defined editor condition and assess combined recognition- and catalytic-domain variants against their matched parents. These measurements would test the working interpretation and the usefulness of ranking.
scope: No experiment or prospective outcome is reported by this audit.
No new candidate cutoffs, sample inclusion policy, scientific thresholds or statistical methods are introduced.
claims.adjustment: Omit the unsupported predicted effect ordering (top-5 minus bottom-5 greater than any protein variant comparison) and multiplicative rather than additive reduction claim; no recorded result supports either magnitude.

claims.placement: Module 4 conclusion: distinct scopes stated in prose, no new figure
claims.supported_wording: The published decision points use different scopes: a PUF12-derived reference of 899,942 callable cytosines, raw retained candidate counts of 12,908 for PUF12 and 383 for GVE, and a regional ranking budget of ten cytidines with source-reported Hit@10 of 77.9% in 140 positive test regions. These are not successive nested subsets or one fitted search-space reduction curve.
scope: The callable reference is defined using PUF12 and three control groups for chromosome normalization.
The raw retained-set counts are not both fully contained in that reference; reference intersections are 12,903 for PUF12 and 376 for GVE.
GVE and PUF12 are separate editor results, not successive filtering steps on one common retained-site set.
Ten candidates is a per-region budget, not a transcriptome-wide site count; Hit@10 is a conditional region-level success fraction.
Apparent C388 includes endogenous reference T.
claims.adjustment: Use nonnested decision-point cards or panels, not a log funnel or waterfall claiming a single denominator. Figure S1 also needs independent axes: measured-versus-predicted S and local ratio are not unwanted burden versus retained activity on one shared scale.

claims.supported_wording: GVE retained 383 candidate sites, approximately 97.0% fewer than PUF12, while retaining an apparent C388 signal of 64.98%. This is a narrower detected candidate profile under the published HEK293T screening procedure and a concrete lead for further evaluation, not a demonstrated therapeutic benefit or toxicity reduction.
scope: Apparent C388 includes endogenous T and cannot serve as effective APOE4 transcript conversion fraction.
Each median summarizes a different retained-site set; count multiplied by median is not an observed total editing burden, molecular exposure or clinical toxicity measure.
Cell data come from HEK293T; cell-type, expression, coverage and delivery effects limit clinical extrapolation.
A target-to-comparison ratio in Module 3 cannot place the triple-mutant direction on a therapeutic window without matched broad profiling and conversion measurements.
claims.adjustment: Preserve the quantitative candidate-set improvement with limitations; do not translate these counts into therapeutic benefit/risk curves or claim field-calibrated clinical success.

terminology.ORCA: On-target RNA Correction for Alzheimer’s Disease; project name
terminology.APOBEC: Catalytic-domain component; assay-specific preference/activity outputs do not alone establish transcriptome-wide specificity
terminology.LAMAR: RNA foundation-model workflow adapted for region assessment and cytidine ranking
terminology.apparent C388: Reported signal includes endogenous reference T; not isolated transgene conversion efficiency
terminology.retained candidate sites: Sites passing the published RNA-seq screening procedure; not individually validated clinical off-targets
